title: Tilenus: the schools confuse the gifts with justifying grace
source_text: XIII. Porro Tilenus hac in parte non videtur aliud in Scholasticis reprehendere, quam quod dona illa quae vocant gratiam gratum facientem, confundant cum gratia justificante & salvante, quae ex Theologorum Reformatorum sententia, non est aliquid in nobis inhaerens, sed tantum gratia Dei activa & externa. Loquens enim de spe, fide & charitate, Hanc gratiam, inquit, gratum facientem vocant Scholastici, & cum illa ἐνεργητικῇ periculosissime confundunt. Thesi illa 22. saepius citatae disputationis de variis divinae voluntatis nominibus.
pass_a_gloss: XIII. Further Tilenus in this part does not seem to reprehend anything else in the Scholastics, than that those gifts which they call grace making pleasing, they confuse with justifying and saving grace, which from the opinion of the Reformed Theologians, is not anything inhering in us, but only the active and external grace of God. For speaking of hope, faith and charity, This grace, he says, the Scholastics call making pleasing, and most dangerously confuse it with that active one. In that thesis 22. of the disputation on the various names of the divine will more often cited.
pass_b_english: Thesis XIII. On this point Tilenus seems to fault the scholastics for one thing only. They confuse the gifts they call grace that makes pleasing with justifying and saving grace, which in the view of the Reformed theologians is not anything inhering in us but simply God's active and external grace.

Speaking of hope, faith and love, he says: The scholastics call this grace that makes pleasing, and most dangerously confuse it with that active grace. This is in thesis 22 of the often-cited disputation on the various names of the divine will.

lemmas.gloss: they confuse with justifying and saving grace
only the active and external grace of God

choices.why: Greek adjective, feminine dative agreeing with an understood gratia: grace as God's own working, the 'active' sense of Thesis I. Read from an enlarged scan of PDF 528; the djvu text garbles it.
